description:
Scenario: RFC 9610 §2.3 mandates two forbidden-class checks on AddressBook/set:

 1. The shareWith property may only be set by users with the 'mayShare' right.
 2. When modifying shareWith, the user cannot grant a right to a Principal that the Principal does not already have AND that the user making the change also does not have.
 3. Users can subscribe/unsubscribe via isSubscribed; the server MAY forbid subscriptions to certain books even with permission, rejecting with 'forbidden' SetError.

None of these are implemented in handle_address_book_set. There is no shareWith-write check, no rights-vs-rights cross-validation, and no isSubscribed allow/deny hook. The reference MemoryBackend also has none of these — it stores whatever is given.

This is consistent with the workspace pattern 'backends are canonical for permission enforcement' — the handler shouldn't do auth, the backend should. But the workspace's caller-identity foundation seam (JmapBackend::principal_id) is not used at all in this crate. Backends that wire principal_id can implement these checks; backends that don't (the default and MemoryBackend) silently allow everything. That's the workspace's documented contract for single-user / fixture backends.

The maintenance consequence: the BACKENDS that consumers ship with their products will need to implement four distinct enforcement paths (shareWith write, rights-cross-validation, isSubscribed allow, plus the existing addressBookHasContents). The contacts-server PLAN.md or AGENTS.md should call this out explicitly as 'consumer responsibility — these checks are not enforced by the handler, your backend must do them'. Without that documentation, a consumer integrating against this crate may not realize the checks are missing.

Recommendation: add a 'Permission enforcement responsibilities' section to PLAN.md or README enumerating all the §2.3 / §3 checks the consumer's backend must perform. Optionally, add example test cases against MemoryBackend that demonstrate the gap (e.g. 'integration test for shareWith write IS allowed by reference MemoryBackend; production backends must override').
title: AddressBook/set shareWith / mayShare 'forbidden' enforcement not implemented in handler or reference backend
